Definition: a horse (as leaping); also a swallow (from its rapid flight)
BiblicalUsage: The horse is the strength of Egypt and the pride of kings, and Pharaoh's horses pursue Israel into the sea. The plague falls on the horses, and the song of Moses celebrates the horse and rider thrown into the sea. Joshua meets kings with horses and chariots as many as the sand, and the word is always a picture of power that cannot save.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the horse in Scripture is the test of trust: will you trust the chariot, or the God who throws it into the sea? Egypt's horses drowned, and Canaan's horses were hamstrung, because God fights for His people. My position is that every horse in the Bible asks the same question, and the right answer is always the LORD.
